Rashi on Keritot 5a:10:1.hebrew: הפגול א' מגופי תורה - דחייבין עליו כרת, ולא למדוה הכתוב שיהא בכרת, אלא נאמר בקדושים תהיו "ואוכליו עונו ישא". ואע"ג דכתיב ביה "פגול", לא בפיגול גמור קמיירי, אלא במחשב בשחיטה חוץ למקומו, דהכי דרשינן בתורת כהנים ובשחיטת קדשים (דף כח:): "אם אינו ענין לחוץ לזמנו, תנהו ענין לחוץ למקומו". וליכא למימר דהאי כרת עליה קאי, דכתיב בפגול גמור בצו את אהרן "והנפש האוכלת ממנו עונה תשא", ודרשינן בתורת כהנים: "ממנו" — עונה תשא, ולא מחברו, דהיינו חוץ למקומו דכתיב ביה מחשבה כותיה:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:10:1.english: Piggul is one of the fundamental principles of the Torah - in that one is liable to karet for [eating] it, yet Scripture did not teach it [explicitly] that it should be [punished] with karet; rather, it is stated in [the Torah portion] Kedoshim Tihyu: "And he who eats it shall bear his iniquity" [Leviticus 19:8, followed by karet]. And even though "piggul" is written in [that passage], [Scripture] is not speaking of actual piggul, but rather of one who intends during slaughter [to eat the offering] outside its proper place, for so we expound in Torat Kohanim and in [Tractate] Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim] (28b): "If it has no application to [intent] outside its proper time, apply it to [intent] outside its proper place." And one cannot say that this karet refers to [intent outside its proper place], because it is written regarding actual piggul in [the Torah portion] Tzav et Aharon: "And the soul that eats from it shall bear its iniquity" [Leviticus 7:18], and we expound in Torat Kohanim: "[From] it" — it shall bear its iniquity, and not [from] its fellow, which is [an offering intended to be eaten] outside its proper place, regarding which [improper] intent is written just like it.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:11:1.hebrew: ונאמר להלן - גבי נותר בפרשת קדושים תהיו, "ואוכליו עונו ישא" וגו'. מה (כאן) [להלן] בקדושים תהיו כרת, דכתיב "ונכרת":
Rashi on Keritot 5a:11:1.english: And it is stated there - Regarding notar, in the Torah portion of Kedoshim Tihyu: “And everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity,” etc. Just as [the punishment] there, in Kedoshim Tihyu, is karet, as it is written: “and [that soul] shall be cut off.”

Rashi on Keritot 5a:11:2.hebrew: נאמר כאן - בצו את אהרן בפגול גמור, והנפש האוכלת וגו', והתם כתיב לא יחשב, דהיינו פגול גמור חוץ לזמנו:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:11:2.english: It is stated here - In [the Torah portion] Tzav et Aharon, regarding complete piggul: “And the soul that eats, etc.”; and there it is written, “it shall not be accepted,” which is complete piggul, [namely] beyond its [appointed] time.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:12:1.hebrew: ולא למדו הכתוב - לנותר בכרת אלא בגזירה שוה, דלא ידעינן דהאי כרת דקדושים תהיו בנותר קמיירי, דהא בתר דקרא דחוץ למקומו כתיב ומשמע דעליה קאי, אלא משום דאתיא קדש קדש:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:12:1.english: And the verse did not teach it - [namely,] notar [being punishable] with karet, except through a verbal analogy; for we would not know that this karet of [Parashat] Kedoshim refers to notar, since it is written after the verse of [an offering eaten] outside its [proper] place and it implies that it refers to it, were it not that [the verbal analogy of] kodesh, kodesh is derived.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:14:1.english: His daughter from a woman he raped [is] one of the fundamentals of the Torah - For [it is punishable] by burning.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:15:1.hebrew: אתיא הנה הנה - כתיב באשתו (ויקרא י״ח:י״ז): ערות אשה ובתה לא תגלה, דמשמע בתה ממנו ובתה מאחר; סיפיה דקרא: שארה הנה זמה היא. וכתיב (שם): ערות בת בנך או בת בתך, ובאנוסה כתיב, דהא בת בתו מאשתו נפקא לו מקרא דלעיל: ערות אשה ובתה; ובתו לא כתיבא באנוסתו, אלא אתיא הנה הנה מאשתו. כתיב באשתו: שארה הנה זמה היא, וכתיב באנוסתו: כי ערותך הנה; מה התם כתיבא בתו, דכתיב אשה ובתה, אף כאן נמי באנוסה עשה בתו כבת בתו. וא"ת: קל וחומר הוא? אין מזהירין מן הדין:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:15:1.english: [It is] derived [from] “they [henna]” “they [henna]” - It is written with regard to one’s wife (Leviticus 18:17): “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover,” which implies [both] her daughter from him and her daughter from another [man]; [and] the end of the verse [states]: “They [henna] are near kinswomen; it is lewdness.” And it is written (ibid.): “The nakedness of your son’s daughter, or of your daughter’s daughter,” and it is written with regard to a woman he raped, for his daughter’s daughter from his wife is [already] derived from the verse above: “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter”; but his daughter is not written [explicitly] with regard to the woman he raped; rather, it is derived [via] “they [henna]” “they [henna]” from [the verse regarding] his wife. It is written with regard to his wife: “They [henna] are near kinswomen; it is lewdness,” and it is written with regard to the woman he raped: “For they [henna] are your own nakedness”; just as there his daughter is written, as it is written “a woman and her daughter,” so too here, with regard to a woman he raped, [Scripture] treated his daughter like his daughter’s daughter. And if you say: It is an a fortiori inference [kal vachomer]? We do not derive a prohibition from a logical inference.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:16:1.english: “Lewdness,” “lewdness,” for burning - [As it is written:] “If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is lewdness” (Leviticus 20:14).

Rashi on Keritot 5a:17:1.hebrew: נסקלין - רוב חייבי סקילה, כגון הבא על האם ועל הכלה, לא כתיבא סקילה, אלא דמיהם בם (שם):
Rashi on Keritot 5a:17:1.english: Those who are stoned - [For] most of those liable to stoning, such as one who has relations with his mother or with his daughter-in-law, stoning is not written [in the verse], rather "their blood is upon them" (there).

Rashi on Keritot 5a:19:1.hebrew: המפטם - לסוך ממנו, חייב, דכתיב (שמות ל׳:ל״ג) אשר ירקח כמוהו:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:19:1.english: One who blends - [in order] to anoint [himself] with it is liable, as it is written (Exodus 30:33): "Whoever compounds [any] like it."

Rashi on Keritot 5a:19:2.english: And one who applies from it - Another [person] who did not blend it.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:19:3.hebrew: ואשר יתן ממנו - מאותו של משה:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:19:3.english: And whoever puts any of it - From that [oil] of Moses.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:21:1.hebrew: לחצאין - כגון ו' לוגין, דההוא דמשה הוה הין, י"ב לוגין:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:21:1.english: In halves - For example, six logs, for that [oil] of Moses was a hin, [which is] twelve logs.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:21:2.hebrew: חצאין דקטרת - קפ"ד מנין, דבכל יום היה מקטיר מנה, כדאמרינן לקמן (כריתות ד' ו.) שס"ה מנין (כמנין ימות החמה):
Rashi on Keritot 5a:21:2.english: Halves of incense - [That is,] 184 manehs, for every day he would burn a maneh, as we say below (Keritot 6a) [that the full amount was] 365 manehs (corresponding to the number of days of the solar year).

Rashi on Keritot 5a:22:1.english: A portion in the morning - Half a maneh.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:23:2.hebrew: קנמן בשם ה' מאות - דהכי אמר קרא: "מחציתו חמשים ומאתים", דלהכי נקט "מחציתו", שלא יהו שוקלים אותו הכל ביחד, אלא לחצאין, כדי שיהו שם שתי הכרעות:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:23:2.english: Aromatic cinnamon, five hundred [shekels] - For thus the verse states: "Half of it, two hundred and fifty" [Exodus 30:23]; for this reason it states "half of it" — so that they should not weigh it all together, but rather in halves, so that there would be two overweights [on the scale].

Rashi on Keritot 5a:24:1.hebrew: תנא הכי קשיא ליה - כלומר, להכי אשמעינן ברייתא, דאי ממשמעותא דקרא הוה אמינא קנה בושם כקנמן בשם, דמחציתו דקרא אתרוייהו קאי; קמ"ל:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:24:1.english: This is difficult for the tanna - That is to say, for this [reason] the baraita taught us [the total], for if [we deduced it] from the plain meaning of the verse, I would have said [that] aromatic calamus [is] like aromatic cinnamon, as [the word] "half of it" in the verse refers to both of them; [therefore, it] teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Keritot 5a:25:1.english: Half to half - That they would weigh [them] in halves.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:26:1.english: With precision - That the spice does not tip [the scale].

Rashi on Keritot 5a:26:2.hebrew: (ע"א) המקום יודע בהכרעות - שלא היה שוקל ההכרעות לבד, אלא מניחן כמות שהן, והמקום יודע מה משקלו. פירוש רומי:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:26:2.english: The Omnipresent knows the surpluses - For he would not weigh the surpluses separately, rather, he would leave them as they were, and the Omnipresent knows what its weight is. [From the] Roman commentary.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:27:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב יהודה הכי קשיא ליה כו' - ה"ג אלא אמר רב יהודה - מדקא מייתי ליה תרי זימני, ודאי לאפושי הוא דעבד:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:27:1.english: Rather, Rav Yehuda said, this was difficult for him, etc. - We read: Rather, Rav Yehuda said — since he brings it two times, he certainly did [so] to increase [the amount].

Rashi on Keritot 5a:28:1.hebrew: שלא יניח משקל כו' - שישקול כל בשם ובשם כנגד הברזל, ולא ישקול במניין דמר דרור ויחזור וישקול קדה כנגד מר דרור:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:28:1.english: That one should not place a weight, etc. - That he must weigh each and every spice against the iron [weight], and he should not weigh with the measure of pure myrrh and then go back and weigh cassia against the pure myrrh.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:29:2.hebrew: אינו סיפק - דשמן לא הוה אלא י"ב לוגין, ועיקרין הוו טובא:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:29:2.english: Is not sufficient - For the oil was only twelve log, and the roots were very many.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:29:3.hebrew: ושראן במים - שיבלעו המים, ולכשיציף עליהן השמן, לא יבלעוהו:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:29:3.english: And soaked them in water - So that they would absorb the water, and when he floated the oil over them, they would not absorb it.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:29:4.hebrew: וקלט השמן את הריח וקפחו - קנחו, וחברו "קפחת את הרועה" ביומא (דף פג:). קנחו משה לשמן מעל העיקרין ונתנו בצלוחית:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:29:4.english: And the oil absorbed the fragrance, and he removed it - He skimmed it off, and its cognate [usage is] "You have cleaned out the shepherd" in [Tractate] Yoma (83b). Moses skimmed the oil off the top of the roots and placed it in a flask.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:2:1.hebrew: נכתוב לא תוכל לאכלם - דהא איירי לעיל, עולותיכם וזבחיכם מעשרותיכם וגו':
Rashi on Keritot 5a:2:1.english: Let [Scripture] write, "You may not eat them" - For it spoke above [of], "your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, etc."

Rashi on Keritot 5a:3:1.english: Bread, parched grain, and fresh stalks - Before the omer [offering].

Rashi on Keritot 5a:3:2.english: Parched grain - That was dried in an oven.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:3:3.english: Fresh stalks - [Grain] that was rubbed by hand and was not singed in fire.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:5:1.hebrew: קלי וכרמל איתנהו בעינייהו, דלא טחנן:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:5:1.english: Parched grain and fresh stalks are in their unadulterated form, since they have not been ground.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:5:2.hebrew: קלי נתרבה - במנחת העומר, דכתיב גביה (ויקרא ב) "קלוי באש". ואף על גב דבההוא קרא כתיב "כרמל", לא הוכשר אלא על ידי האור, כדאמרינן במנחות (דף סו:): אבוב של קליות היה שם מנוקב ככברה, שיהא האור שולט בכולן. ולשון "כרמל": רך ומל — רך שנמלל:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:5:2.english: Parched grain has an increased [obligation] - In the omer meal offering, concerning which it is written (Leviticus 2): "parched with fire." And even though "fresh stalks" [karmel] is [also] written in that verse, it is only rendered fit [for the offering] through fire, as we say in Menachot (66b): There was a pipe for parching there, perforated like a sieve, so that the fire would take hold of all of them. And the meaning of karmel is rakh u-mal — tender [grain] that has been crushed.

Rashi on Keritot 5a:6:1.hebrew: לחם ישנו במנחות, דלחם הפנים איקרי מנחה, ושתי הלחם של עצרת, דכתיב בהו (במדבר כח) "בהקריבכם מנחה חדשה":
Rashi on Keritot 5a:6:1.english: Bread is [included] among meal offerings, for the Showbread is called a meal offering, and [so too] the Two Loaves of Shavuot, as it is written concerning them (Numbers 28): "When you bring a new meal offering."

Rashi on Keritot 5a:7:1.hebrew: שכן איתנהו בעינייהו - הלכך, לא מצית ילפת לה, דהא כי אמרינן "מה לקלי דאיתיה בעיניה", ליכא למימר "כרמל יוכיח":
Rashi on Keritot 5a:7:1.english: For they are in their [natural] form - Therefore, you cannot derive it [i.e., bread], for when we say, "What [is unique] about parched grain, that it is in its [natural] form," one cannot say, "Fresh stalks will prove [otherwise]."

Rashi on Keritot 5a:7:2.hebrew: שכן נתרבו אצל מנחות - וכי פרכת מה לקלי שכן נתרבה על ידי מנחות, ליכא למימר לחם יוכיח:
Rashi on Keritot 5a:7:2.english: In that they were included with regard to meal offerings - And if you refute [it by asking]: What [is unique] about parched grain, in that it was included through meal offerings? One cannot say, 'Bread will prove [it]!'
